newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican grain warehouse auctions on the block soon.
newsitem.headline: Mexican grain warehouse auctions on the block soon.

text.p: Mexico is proceeding with its privatization of the country's state-owned grains warehouses and winners of the first phase sell-off will be announced soon, Ixe Banco said Monday.
Ixe Banco, the banking arm of financial firm Ixe Grupo Financiero, is the privatization agent designated by the Finance Ministry to auction off the warehouses known in Mexico as ANDSA.
Plans are to sell off three packages of the 80-some warehouse units in three phases, starting with a package centered around the southern state of Veracruz.

The privatization of Almacenadora Sur (Southern Warehouses) will be concluded soon, Ixe said in a statement giving no further details. Ixe spokesmen were not immediately available to define when an announcement will be made.

Ixe said in its statement that the register for the auction of Servicios de Almacenamiento del Norte (Northern Warehouse Services) was started Monday and the sell-off should be completed by September.

Northern Warehouse Services is the second package of warehouses to be put on the block. Included in the package is the partial assignment of the rights for the use and operation of grains silos in Guaymas, a port in northwest Mexico.
The third and final package to be auctioned off will be Almacenadora Centro Occidente (Central West Warehouses). Ixe gave no timetable for its privatization.

"Under the terms of the sell-off, it is stressed that in the case of equal bids preference will be given to the bid that includes the participation of up to 20 percent (share holding) by an organisation of farmers," IXe said.
Foreign participation in the sell-off can be up to 49 percent of the share package. Winners of the Almacenadora Sur auction cannot take part in following sell-offs, Ixe said.

ANDSA's warehouses have a combined total storage capacity of 4.5 million tonnes of grains. The packages at auction are centered in the geographical regions implicit in their names, but also have scattered national presence.
((--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com))
